dedupe_keys.name: cards california residential water demand and supply open dataset 2013 2021

description: CaRDS is a statewide open dataset of monthly water supply and residential water demand for 404 water suppliers in California, compiled by the authors from open-access sources and described in a Scientific Data descriptor. Each supplier, keyed by its public water system identifier, has monthly supply, residential demand, mean temperature, cumulative precipitation and Palmer Drought Severity Index series, and a supplier file gives location, hydrologic and climatic zones, population served and size. Coverage is California, United States, 2013 to 2021. The data are a free download from HydroShare under CC BY 4.0 as CSV files, with the Jupyter notebooks that build them. Caveats: supply is water produced, not delivered, so storage can add lags, and demand is water billed to residential customers, which depends on metering; the data are largely based on survey reports. Simulation uses: demand scenarios and drought response analysis for water supply capacity planning. Related records: the USGS public supply water use reanalysis (data-usgs-public-supply-water-use-reanalysis-huc12) and Tethys water demand (data-tethys-conus-gridded-water-demand-1980-2100).
